## Introduction 

In this notebook, we are reverse engineering the story, [Thousands of kids are missing from school. Where did they go?](https://projects.apnews.com/features/2023/missing-children/index.html)

## Load libraries

Loading required libraries for this analysis.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
  options(scipen=999)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(janitor)
  library(dplyr)

```

## Load and Cleaning Data

In this section, describe the source of the data, write a basic data dictionary for data you are working with, and discuss any caveats or issues you discovered working with this data. 

```{r}
# Load required data

age_pop <- read.csv("data/population-by-age.csv") |> clean_names()
public_enrollment <- read.csv("data/public-enrollment-by-grade.csv") |> clean_names()
private_enrollment <- read.csv("data/private-enrollment-by-grade.csv") |> clean_names ()

# Path to data should be loaded from folder "data" i.e. read_csv("data/name_of_data.csv")

# Clean required data and prepare for analysis if needed. 

clean_public_enrollment <- public_enrollment |> rename(state_ab = "st", public_enrollment = "enrollment")

clean_private_enrollment <- private_enrollment |> 
  rename( private_enrollment = "enrollment", state_ab = "state")

school_story <- clean_public_enrollment |> full_join(clean_private_enrollment, join_by(fips, sch_year, grade, state_ab)) |>
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12))
  

```

## Sentences to Engineer
In this notebook, we are reverse engineering five sentences from the story.

### Sentence 1

* **Sentence text**:  “The population of school-age kids in the states we studied fell by about 183,000, according to census estimates.” 

* **Analysis summary**: Our results confirmed the AP's claim that the population of school-age kids in the 22 states studied fell by about 183,000. We found this number by comparing the provided age and population data from July 2020 to the age and population data we have from July 2021. 


```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here
twenty_age_pop <- age_pop |>
  mutate(year=year(est_date), month = month(est_date)) |>
  filter(year == 2020 & month == 4) |>
 filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarize(total_pop_20=sum(population))

twenty_one_age_pop <- age_pop |>
  mutate(year=year(est_date), month = month(est_date)) |>
  filter(year == 2021 & month ==7) |>
 filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarize(total_pop_21=sum(population))

#change <- states_age_pop |>
 # pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = total) |>
 # rename(twenty="2020", twenty_one="2021") |>
 # mutate(change = twenty_one - twenty ) |>
 # mutate(total_change=sum(change)) |>
 # arrange(desc(change))
  

# twenty_age_pop<- age_pop |>   mutate(year=year(est_date)) |>
 # filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12) & (year == 2020)) |> group_by(year) |> summarize(total=sum(population))

# twenty_one_age_pop<- age_pop |>   mutate(year=year(est_date)) |>
 # filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12) & (year == 2021)) |> group_by(year) |> summarize(total=sum(population))

combo_age_year_change <- twenty_one_age_pop |>
  left_join(twenty_age_pop, join_by(state)) |>
  mutate(change = total_pop_20 - total_pop_21) |>
  summarize(total_change = sum(change))

# Display results of code below this codeblock

combo_age_year_change
```
